short: Nigeria has no AI statute. The National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, 2025 contains a binding AI chapter enforced by NITDA; meanwhile the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 binds, with fines of up to 2% of annual gross revenue.
title: Nigeria AI Laws
subtitle: An AI chapter in the Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, and the Data Protection Act that binds
body_html:
Status at a glance

AI bill pending. Nigeria has no AI statute. The National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, 2025, before the National Assembly, contains a binding chapter on artificial intelligence (ss. 63 to 69) that would make the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) the AI regulator. Until it is enacted, AI that processes personal data is governed by the Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023, whose section 37 gives a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions. Verified on 25 October 2026 against the National Assembly, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission and NITDA.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberDateStatus
National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, 2025National Assembly bill document 11219 (Senate, 10th Assembly)2025Not enacted
Nigeria Data Protection Act, 20232023 No. 37Commencement 12 June 2023In force
National Artificial Intelligence StrategyNCAIR/NITDA draft2024Draft policy

Who regulates and enforces

  • National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA): the regulatory agency for AI under the bill (ss. 66 to 68).
  • Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC): enforces the Data Protection Act, including section 37 on automated decisions.

Scope and reach

The bill would reach any person or public institution that develops, deploys or uses an AI system (s. 63), and "artificial intelligence agents" (s. 2). The Data Protection Act already reaches controllers and processors outside Nigeria that process the personal data of a data subject in Nigeria (s. 2(2)(c)).

Core obligations

  • Under the bill, if enacted: AI must be fair, transparent and explainable, safe, accountable, contestable, under human oversight and compliant with the Data Protection Act (s. 63(1)); risk-proportionate governance and impact assessment, user information, bias safeguards, audit records and disclosure of the operator's identity (s. 64(1)); risk classification by NITDA regulation (s. 65); an annual system impact assessment report (s. 69).
  • Today: the Data Protection Act, including the right not to be subject to solely automated decisions, with human intervention and a right to contest (s. 37).

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Data Protection Act infringements by a controller or processor of major importanceThe greater of NGN 10,000,000 and 2% of annual gross revenue in the preceding financial yearNDPA s. 48(4)NDPC
Other Data Protection Act infringementsThe greater of NGN 2,000,000 and 2% of annual gross revenueNDPA s. 48(5)NDPC
An AI agent violating the bill or its regulations, if enactedThe higher of 10,000,000 (no currency is stated in the text) and 2% of annual gross revenue from NigeriaBill s. 68(2)(d)NITDA

What is coming next

  • The bill's remaining stages and presidential assent; no official date was found, and the National Assembly's bill tracker does not show the stage.

Sources

  • National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, 2025, National Assembly
  • Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023, NDPC
  • National AI Strategy (draft), NCAIR and NITDA

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: the bill's current stage, which the press reported as a third reading in July 2026, and whether the National AI Strategy was adopted beyond its 2024 draft.
